title: A dead star 1,000 light-years away sprays a jet that flails like a loose fire hose

cover.alt: Chandra X-ray image of the Vela pulsar: a glowing blue crescent around a bright white dot, with a faint wiggly jet reaching up to the right.
cover.credit: NASA/CXC/Univ of Toronto/M. Durant et al. · Public domain

body: The Vela pulsar is a neutron star, the collapsed core left after a massive star exploded more than 10,000 years ago. It is only about 19 km across but spins more than **11 times a second**, faster than a helicopter rotor. Along its spin axis it fires out a jet of charged particles at about 70% of the speed of light, and NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory has watched the 0.7-light-year-long jet bend and whip around from one image to the next. Its corkscrew shape suggests the pulsar may be wobbling slightly as it spins, like a top.

slides.alt: A glowing blue crescent of X-ray light around a bright white dot, with a faint, thin jet curving up and to the right that wiggles and changes shape over and over.
slides.caption: Eight Chandra X-ray images of the Vela pulsar taken from June to September 2010, played as a repeating loop: the faint jet at upper right bends and whips around.
slides.credit: NASA/CXC/Univ of Toronto/M. Durant et al. · Public domain · excerpt, cropped

slides.question: The Vela pulsar is a ball about 19 km across. How many times does it spin every second?
slides.explanation: More than 11 full turns every second, faster than a helicopter rotor, for an object about as wide as a city.

slides.heading: How big the cloud left by the star’s explosion looks in our sky
slides.note: The cloud from the explosion is about 8 degrees across, 16 times the Moon’s apparent size

left.label: Earth
left.text: Its spin axis slowly circles around once every 26,000 years or so.

right.label: Vela pulsar
right.text: If it is wobbling, astronomers estimate one circle takes only about 120 days.

slides.question: How fast do the particles in the Vela pulsar’s jet travel?
slides.explanation: The charged particles race out along the pulsar’s spin axis at about 70% of the speed of light.

source.label: Chandra: Vela Pulsar Jet, New Chandra Movie Features Neutron Star Action
